gate_reasoning: Stage 2 scores 64.9% Low confidence across 77 scored claims — well above the remediation threshold. The High-confidence spine is solid: cargo theft statistics rest on primary-tier sources (Verisk CargoNet, BSI/TT Club, TIA industry association, Armstrong & Associates, Uber/E2open SEC filings, Trimble IR). The structural problems are (1) pervasive auto-low-vendor captures for product capability claims — Truckstop, Highway, project44, Loadsure, Overhaul, and Transfix metrics are all self-reported in vendor marketing materials without independent audit; (2) all market-sizing figures for TMS, SEA road freight, and freight procurement software TAM derive from auto-downgraded aggregators (MarketsandMarkets, Mordor, Grand View, MarkNtel, DataIntelo); (3) 15 ASSUMED-tagged claims require field validation before they should appear in a delivered report; and (4) a material internal inconsistency exists between the BSI/TT Club 18% strategic theft share (High confidence) and the transcredit.com 35%+ figure (Low confidence) for the same metric, which must be resolved. The corpus is not shippable as-is to a client because the most frequently-cited claims — vendor performance metrics, per-load insurance prevalence, SEA market size, spot-market theft rate differential — are uniformly Low or ASSUMED. Deep research should prioritize: (a) an independent cross-reference for the $273,990 Q1 2025 per-incident figure back to primary CargoNet/BSI data; (b) an independent insurance industry source for the cargo underinsurance prevalence figure; (c) FMCSA or TIA primary data for the broker fraud-loss aggregate to replace trade-press-only citations; and (d) a Form D or Crunchbase Pro confirmation for funding rounds currently sourced only from vendor press releases.
